# Changelog

Every release of [allmiibo-sync](https://allmiibo.mathieu.dev), newest first.
The same history, minus the sections that only concern this repository, is on
the site under [What's new](https://allmiibo.mathieu.dev/changelog.html).

## 1.0.0 · 2 August 2026

**First public release**

### Added

#### Libraries in one file

- An all-in-one `.bin` holding a whole library is now a source. Drop it in your folder and it is unpacked during the normal scan, each amiibo planned individually
- Only what is missing transfers. A record is skipped if you already have it in your folder, already have it on the device, or it appeared earlier in the same file
- **PACK FOLDER** and **PACK DEVICE** write one back out
- **FCA archives** are read too, following the format’s published spec. It is the better of the two where you have the choice, because it keeps whole 2048-byte dumps, so Air Riders vehicles survive
- Known limitation, stated plainly: an all-in-one record holds 540 bytes and the Air Riders vehicle sits beyond that, so a character’s four pairings collapse into one vehicle-less entry. A real dump you already hold is never replaced by a bundle copy

#### Picking files instead of a folder

- Pick a loose `.bin` or an all-in-one file directly, without building a folder around it first
- Picked files are read-only: they fill in your collection and can be sent to a device, but downloads and two-way sync still need a real folder
- A picked file keeps the name it arrived with and only gains a series folder

#### Repair and organise

- **REPAIR**, on the debug page, for a folder the device will not finish listing. It reads as far as the device manages, moves those files out in batches of fifty, and asks again. Each pass reaches further because the folder is shorter
- Nothing is deleted and nothing leaves the device during a rescue, so no folder on your computer is needed
- Erasing the folder afterwards is a separate, confirmed step, and it says plainly whether anything was actually rescued. If the device could read nothing, erasing destroys files nobody has seen, and the dialog says exactly that
- **ORGANISE DEVICE** and **ORGANISE FOLDER** give every dump the name and folder the app would have chosen. This is also the cure for the folder shape that causes the problem above
- Organise moves files, never copies or deletes them, and clears away only the folders its own moves emptied
- Anything it cannot recognise is listed and left where it is. A second dump of an amiibo that already claimed its name is reported rather than silently renamed
- `amiibolink/` and `chameleon/` are never touched, since those hold real dumps and refiling them would break slot emulation
- **WIPE** empties a device folder and writes nothing back. It keeps the signing keys and device settings, because deleting those breaks the device rather than emptying it
- **DELETE FROM DEVICE** on a selection, which counts files rather than amiibo and names the ones that expand. Picking one Happy Home Designer card really does mean deleting all 91
- If a repair left files parked on your device, connecting offers to organise, back up or delete them. That folder is a sibling of your device folder, so no ordinary scan would ever mention it

#### Elsewhere

- Amiibo names, series and artwork are now curated rather than taken raw from upstream, including corrected series names, series artwork, and pinned filenames
- A guided tour on the Collection and Advanced sync, shown once and replayable from NEED HELP?
- Troubleshooting in HOW TO, covering the debug tools and what to do when a scan sticks
- Two new amiibo arrived from upstream

### Fixed

- **A slow device timed out on every scan and sync died before a byte moved.** The deadline measured how long a reply took rather than how long the device had been silent, so a large folder was killed part way through a perfectly healthy transfer
- **A folder the app could not read was treated as an empty one and removed**, and removing a folder on the device takes its contents with it. It could not have been noticed from the outside, and it was already live
- **Renaming a series took the whole site down.** Not a broken thumbnail: no page at all, on every page, because the site imported a table a separate process had not written yet
- **Four Air Riders dumps of one character were saved over each other**, because a name built from the database put all four on one path and kept the last
- **A file the app had just written could not be read back**, because one malformed record rejected the whole thing
- A bundle used to look like an ordinary file, so a sync would have spent minutes pushing something the device cannot read
- A collection of Happy Home Designer cards read as mostly unrecognised
- A reorganise of your own folder estimated itself at zero seconds, which reads as nothing to do

### Behind the scenes

- The admin service: sign in, edit the library, publish. Its own site, so if it dies the public one does not notice
- A curated overlay merged before names are derived, so curated entries face the same collision gates as upstream ones. Upstream can only warn; the overlay author can fail
- The database generator made callable, with `devicepath.js` and `dbsource.js` extracted so the generator, the server and the admin preview run one implementation
- Upstream refresh reviewed as Track Changes, recording every held-back change so a later update can tell a pin still doing its job from one upstream came round to
- Two silent bugs in the old diff: every release table read as empty, and device-side renames read as harmless
- Artwork reviewed in the same pass, detected in one request with no image bytes, downloaded lazily, declines recording the exact version refused
- Authoring new amiibo and curating series, with the ID decoded as you type
- Backup and restore for the overlay, both through one publish path
- The UI made testable, with the collection grid and detail panel shared, and the site output verified byte-identical
- Two live CSS bugs from class names nobody owned
- Test suite from 15 to 766 across 32 files

## 0.1.1 · 29 July 2026

**What the testers found**

### Added

- The scan report opens with the arithmetic: how many files became how many dumps became how many distinct amiibo
- Every device file the scan cannot identify is given a named reason: an unrecognised size, a read that failed, a folder out of reach, or a device system file
- A Bluetooth read that fails is retried once before a file is recorded as unreadable
- The scan no longer stops at a depth we picked. It descends as far as the device itself can address, so "out of reach" is a fact about the hardware rather than a limit of ours
- **EXPORT SCAN LOG**, which saves what both scans saw as JSON for bug reports: filenames, sizes, IDs and errors, never file contents
- The build id in the footer, so a screenshot says which version you are on

### Fixed

- **A nearly empty device refused every sync.** Free space was read as used space, so a device reporting 1,918,644 bytes free of 1,920,401 came out as 1,757 bytes free and rejected everything
- **Refreshing a file already on the device was charged as though it needed room for a second copy**, so an in-place update could be blocked for space it never needed
- **The ONLY ON DEVICE count showed every file on the device** when no folder was connected, restating the total rather than telling you anything. It now appears only when both sides exist and actually differ
- **EXPORT SCAN LOG did nothing on Android Chrome.** The download was silently cancelled; it now works, and a failure says so instead of staying quiet

## 0.1.0 · 26 July 2026

**Private beta**

### Added

#### Your collection

- Every known amiibo, grouped by series, showing what you hold and what you are missing
- 946 amiibo covered, with release dates from the November 2014 launch wave onward
- Amiibo are recognised by the ID inside each dump, so filenames do not matter
- Artwork for every figure, greyed out until you own it, with a letter placeholder for anything newer than the picture set
- Series headers carry a representative figure, curated by hand: Mario for Smash, Isabelle for Animal Crossing, Link for Zelda
- Sort series by release date or alphabetically, and switch between a compact list and a card grid. Both choices are remembered
- Completion shown per series on its row, with a coloured count and a device count once you have scanned one
- Amiibo the database has never heard of are still listed, named by character where possible, and marked as unlisted
- Where a name came from is always visible: the database first, then your filenames, then the character in the dump. A database name is never overridden by a guess
- The **Happy Home Designer card set** is a curated 947th entry with original card-stack art, its 91 cards identified by NFC UID, shown as `n/91` and as a full card grid on its detail page
- **Kirby Air Riders vehicles** are decoded from the dump and tracked individually, so Kirby and Warp Star is a different thing from Kirby and Wagon Star. Each character shows an `n/4` tally and the whole line-up as a checklist
- A settings toggle hides the fan-made card set for official-only totals
- A detail page per amiibo, with full-resolution art and the ID broken down field by field
- Files that are not amiibo dumps are listed and split into system files and genuinely unrecognised ones, with the recognised dump sizes stated

#### Your device

- Connect an Allmiibo over Bluetooth and read what is on it, with no app to install
- Every drive the device reports is walked, not just the first
- The device’s contents count towards your collection, badged as on-device, before anything is copied anywhere
- The app pings the device every ten seconds of silence so an idle one is less likely to power off mid-session

#### Syncing

- Five named operations rather than a direction plus checkboxes: **BACKUP**, **SYNC**, **MATCH**, **REPLACE** and **CHECK**
- Every run is planned first and shown to you before anything is written
- Transfers resume, so a disconnect part way through picks up where it stopped
- A file that only moved is renamed on the device instead of being uploaded again
- **MATCH** asks whether an amiibo is on the device at all, ignoring folder layout
- **CHECK** reads every file back and reports what differs, changing nothing
- Deletions are always shown, even when switched off, under NOT DELETED
- Time estimates, calibrated rather than guessed
- Every operation is logged with its duration, outcome and the device’s own error code, savable as JSON
- A plan that will not fit says so upfront instead of failing part way through
- Deletions run before uploads when both copies will not fit at once
- A repeat backup skips what it already downloaded, with a force option to re-fetch

#### The interface

- An eight-bit console reskin: Press Start 2P for chrome, system fonts for reading
- An original pixel-art pirate mascot standing on a red NFC dock, in twelve colourways
- Three switchable themes, and an Advanced toggle that keeps the expert layer out of the way
- Preferences applied before first paint, so no flash of the wrong theme
- A title screen you start with ENTER or SPACE
- HOW TO, and a public legal and licensing page
- Read-only folder scanning in Firefox and Safari, where syncing is not available. The panel says so rather than showing dead buttons
- Works down to 320px wide

### Awkward cases handled

- All 91 Happy Home Designer cards share one amiibo ID, so they are told apart by NFC UID rather than collapsing into one entry
- Every Kirby Air Riders character shares one ID across its four vehicles, so the vehicle is read out of the tag’s memory instead
- Device filenames Chrome refuses to create locally, such as a folder ending in a space, are renamed on the way down, and every rename is listed in the plan
- Every dump is exactly 540 bytes, so equal size never proves equal content. Anything undecidable is reported rather than guessed
- Removing a folder on the device takes its contents with it, so files go individually and folders only once empty
- The device silently truncates a path over 63 bytes and reports success, so every path is checked before it is sent
- Signing keys and device settings are never treated as library files
